answer:
For average-risk adults, colorectal cancer screening should begin at **age 45** years, according to the USPSTF recommendation. Screening is advised for individuals aged 45 to 75 years, with options including colonoscopy every 10 years, annual fecal immunochemical test (FIT), or stool DNA-FIT every 1–3 years [USPSTF, 2021]. 

This guidance applies to individuals without increased risk factors (e.g., family history, inherited syndromes, or inflammatory bowel disease). Always confirm with a healthcare provider for personalized recommendations. 

**Source:** Screening for Colorectal Cancer, USPSTF, 2021 [USPSTF, 2021].

results.content: The USPSTF recommends screening for colorectal cancer in all adults aged 45 to 75 years. Screening options include colonoscopy every 10 years, annual FIT testing, or stool DNA-FIT every 1-3 years.
